InStage Virtual Interview
announcements.content:
NEW!  InStageInStage is a cloud-based experiential learning tool designed to make it fun for students to build their career skills.  Students can choose from a library of simulations including job interviews, introducing themselves, presenting, and business pitches. After each practice session, students receive a detailed progress report that shows rate of speech, filler words, volume, and much more.  To book your session, go here : https://www.instage.io/library/fanshawe_career
Get ready to go InStage! The importance of developing your communication soft skills cannot be undervalued. Fanshawe is proud to offer InStage virtual reality sessions to before your contact.  To start your practice session, follow these steps: 1. Book a day and time for your practice session 2. Enter your name and email, and select your simulation (Interviews, Introduction, Freestyle Presentation, or ESL.3. Select an InStage Mode (“Solo mode” to practice on your own, “Group mode” for a group presentation) 4. The software will then send an email to confirm your booking
For more details on what to expect in the session, go to https://bit.ly/3fLHKaCQuestions? Email jobsite@fanshawec.ca

announcements.title: Presentation Announcement
announcements.content:
Dear all
We present on Monday, 8 December, at the scheduled class time. We may continue until we finish all presentations.
We start on time. We follow the FOL list. The order may change, so stay prepared.
Please join using the Zoom link.
Timing• 5 minutes maximum for your presentation (penalties apply if you go over time)• 2 to 5 minutes for questions, based on your selected option
Scores and Confirmation• You receive your final course score after you present• Check your grade on FOL after your presentation• Send me a direct (for your privacy) message on Zoom to confirm your final score• If you have any questions about your marking, wait until the end of all presentations• After finalization, scores cannot change
Grading• Presentation is out of 30, includes your presentation, your report, your code, and one question about your final project• You also have 5 points for the course content questions (📗In class Activity (Question answering) - 2 ) that you can choose one option at the start of your presentation: Option A. Use the average of quizzes and the final exam Option B. Answer two questions, 2.5 points each
Be ready. Stay on time. Follow the time limits. Confirm your score.
Good luck!

announcements.title: Final Exam and Presentation Details
announcements.content:
Dear all,
The final exam will be on 3 December 2025 in the next session. Please be on time.
Exam format• 30 multiple choice questions.• Includes coding questions.• Covers all material from the slides.• You can bring one two sided cheat sheet.• After each quiz, please display the submission confirmation page.
Seating• Sit in the same order as the link shared earlier.• Because the room is full, you do not need to leave an empty seat between each person. • Keep seats empty for anyone absent or late.
After the exam: we will start the final project presentations (only for those ones that we already set as volunteers).
Good luck.

announcements.title: Class Recording and LAST Assignment Reminder
announcements.content:
Hi Luiz Henrique,
Please find the recording link for our last class at the bottom of this message.
A quick reminder that your assignment: Brandwatch Social Listening & Sentiment Analysis Walkthrough is due next Wednesday, December 10. You can find all the details in the Assignments section under the Content menu, and it’s also listed in the Course Calendar on the main page.
Quick assignment instructions:
Choose a brand or company that you'd like to analyze. Select a brand aligned with your mock client business
Utilize the search feature on Brandwatch to conduct a thorough analysis of the chosen brand.
Pay attention to relevant metrics, sentiment analysis, and any significant trends or patterns that emerge from the data.
Using Vimeo's screen recording extension, compile your findings into a comprehensive video walkthrough. Your video should be no longer than 5 minutes and no less than 3 minutes.
In the video, clearly articulate the key insights, trends, and sentiment analysis you discovered during your research.
Provide examples and visual representations of the data to support your analysis. Share your screen or create a slide deck with visuals/screenshots.
Showcase your critical thinking skills by offering meaningful interpretations and implications of the findings.
Ensure your video walkthrough is well-structured, engaging, and professionally presented.
To submit your video, submit the link of your Vimeo to the submission folder
Refer to the class material and recording for a guideline of questions you should answer in your video.
If you have any questions, please don’t hesitate to reach out.
Happy recording!

announcements.title: Social Media Rankings Revealed – What Surprised You?
announcements.content:
Hi Luiz Henrique,
As promised, here’s the full list of the Top Social Media Platforms, ranked by global user data and traffic trends.
Earlier in class, I asked you to guess which platform holds the #1 spot. If you said Facebook, you were correct! With over 3 billion monthly active users, it currently leads in user count. However, when it comes to web traffic, YouTube takes the crown—generating a staggering 40 billion visits per month, making it the most visited social platform worldwide.
This ranking isn’t just trivia—it’s a powerful snapshot of how billions of people connect, share, and consume content. Understanding these platforms is essential for navigating today’s digital world.
Looking forward to hearing what stood out to you.
Happy reading!

announcements.title: Welcome!
announcements.content:
Hey Luiz Henrique!
Welcome to Social Media Analytics (INFO-6155)
My name is Christie Ramos, and I’m thrilled to be your professor this semester. While we meet next week, you can get to know me a bit better by viewing my bio under Instructor Information.
Over the next 14 weeks, we embark on a journey to explore how organizations turn social data into decisions—covering social media foundations, strategy and goal-setting, content (including AI-generated content), measurement, and industry tools. We’ll review Hootsuite and Brandwatch, discuss social listening and sentiment analysis, and examine AI’s capabilities, limits, and safeguards in the social landscape. We will also take a hands-on approach to reporting and metric analysis.
By the end of this course, you’ll be able to define and interpret the metrics that matter, build a measurement and content strategy, use AI-powered tools to create content, and conduct market research that incorporates sentiment analysis and social listening.
Next week we kick off class with our first lecture which will serve as an introduction to myself, the course, and some of the key concepts we'll learn throughout the semester.  Please read the Week 1 Module to gear up for our first class.
Class will take place Tuesday, Sep 9th via Zoom at 6:00PM. Please join our weekly online classroom here.
I’m looking forward to virtually seeing you soon. Let’s make this a rewarding and enriching experience for both of us!
